prompt: A `google_storage_bucket` sets no `project`. Where is it created?

choices.text: In the project gcloud is configured for
choices.why: Terraform reads the provider block, not gcloud's configuration, when project is set there.

choices.text: In the provider's project
choices.why: Right. The provider's project is the default for every resource that does not name its own.

choices.text: In a new project Terraform creates for the configuration, named after the directory
choices.why: Terraform creates nothing it was not told to create.

choices.text: Nowhere: project is required on every resource
choices.why: It is optional on the resource precisely because the provider supplies it.

prompt: Why is `.terraform.lock.hcl` committed with the code?

choices.text: It holds the state, so others can see what exists
choices.why: State is a different file entirely; the lock file holds no resources.

choices.text: It stores the access token for the team
choices.why: No credential is ever written there.

choices.text: So everybody runs the same provider, by checksum
choices.why: Right. A different provider can change what plan means.

choices.text: It stops two people applying at once
choices.why: That is the state lock, lesson 6, not this file.

prompt: What do `default_labels` in the provider block do?

choices.text: Label every resource it creates that takes labels
choices.why: Right. The cheapest way to give every resource an owner.

choices.text: Label only the resources that already declare labels of their own
choices.why: They apply to every resource that accepts labels, declared or not.

choices.text: Label the project itself
choices.why: The project is not created here; resources in it are labelled.

choices.text: Filter which resources Terraform may manage
choices.why: Labels decide nothing about what Terraform manages.

prompt: Put the places the google provider looks for credentials in the order it tries them.
hint: First match wins, from the most explicit to the machine's own.
items: The metadata server of the machine
trap: Putting the metadata server first is the slip: an explicit token or file always wins over the machine.

prompt: `terraform plan` on a new laptop stops with "could not find default credentials". What is the right fix for a person with a Google account?
hint: Which of the four places belongs to a person on a laptop?

choices.text: Download a service account key and set GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
choices.why: A key file is the last resort, a long-lived secret on a laptop.

choices.text: gcloud auth application-default login
choices.why: Right. The person's own short-lived login, refreshed by gcloud.

choices.text: Write the key into the provider's credentials argument
choices.why: Then the key is in the repository, and outlives every rotation.

choices.text: Set GOOGLE_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN=fake
choices.why: That works only against the emulator; Google refuses it.

prompt: Terraform runs in a Cloud Build step. Where should its credentials come from?

choices.text: A key file uploaded to the build's workspace
choices.why: A key would have to be stored somewhere the build can read it, and so can others.

choices.text: An access token pasted into the trigger's substitutions
choices.why: A token expires in an hour and is visible in the trigger's settings.

choices.text: The developer's Application Default Credentials
choices.why: Those live on a laptop, not on a build machine.

choices.text: The metadata server
choices.why: Right. The build's own service account, with nothing stored.

prompt: With `impersonate_service_account` set, what does the person running Terraform need on the production project?
hint: Their own credentials are used for one thing only.

choices.text: Owner, since Terraform changes everything
choices.why: The service account holds the permissions; the person holds almost none.

choices.text: Token Creator on that one service account
choices.why: Right. Nothing on the project itself; taking that role away removes their access.

choices.text: Editor on the project and Token Creator on the account
choices.why: Editor is exactly what impersonation exists to avoid giving.

choices.text: A key for the service account on their laptop
choices.why: Impersonation needs no key at all.

prompt: After the apply, `gcloud` shows the bucket in `US-CENTRAL1` with no labels. Why?

choices.text: default_labels apply only on the second apply
choices.why: They apply on the first; the plan showed them.

choices.text: The token fake is refused for labels
choices.why: Nothing checked the token; the emulator just did not keep them.

choices.text: The emulator keeps neither, and answers defaults
choices.why: Right. Accepted is not the same as done; Google would have kept both.

choices.text: A bucket's location is always US-CENTRAL1 until it is moved
choices.why: A location is set at creation and can never be moved.

prompt: A plan shows `location = "US" -> "SOUTHAMERICA-EAST1" # forces replacement` on a bucket full of data. What would applying it do against Google?
hint: Can a location be changed in place?

choices.text: Move the bucket and its objects to São Paulo
choices.why: Nothing moves a bucket; the provider can only destroy and recreate it.

choices.text: Change the location label and leave the data where it is
choices.why: Location is not a label; it is where the data physically lives.

choices.text: Delete the bucket, with its objects, and make an empty one
choices.why: Right. The line that deserves the slowest reading in any plan.

choices.text: Nothing: Google refuses location changes
choices.why: Google refuses the change in place, which is exactly why the provider replaces.

prompt: Creating a Cloud Run service in a new project fails with `SERVICE_DISABLED`, though the caller is an owner. What is missing?

choices.text: The run.googleapis.com API is off
choices.why: Right. APIs start off; a google_project_service turns it on.

choices.text: A billing account with a budget
choices.why: A missing billing account gives a different error; budgets refuse nothing.

choices.text: The roles/run.admin role, which owner does not include
choices.why: Owner includes it; the API being off is the issue.

choices.text: A region in the provider block
choices.why: A missing region gives a different, explicit error.

prompt: Why does the shop set `disable_on_destroy = false` on its `google_project_service` resources?

choices.text: So that destroy runs faster
choices.why: Speed is not the reason; the side effect is.

choices.text: Because Google charges for turning an API off
choices.why: Turning one off costs nothing in money.

choices.text: Because disabled APIs cannot be enabled again
choices.why: They can; the damage is what stops in between.

choices.text: So tearing this down leaves the API on for everyone else
choices.why: Right. Services this configuration never created would stop too.

prompt: To act as a service account without a key, the provider argument is `___` (one word with underscores).
Which of these belong in the shop's Terraform repository? Choose all that apply.
hint: Code and the lock, yes; secrets and caches, no.

choices.text: main.tf
choices.why: Yes, the configuration.

choices.text: .terraform.lock.hcl
choices.why: Yes, so everyone runs the same provider.

choices.text: .terraform/, the downloaded provider
choices.why: No. init downloads it again from the lock.

choices.text: A service account key file
choices.why: No. Never a key in a repository.

prompt: A configuration manages buckets in `planner-dev` and `planner-prod` with one provider block whose `project` is `planner-dev`. One prod bucket forgot its `project` argument. What happens?
hint: The default fills in what is not written.

choices.text: The plan fails because the bucket's project is ambiguous
choices.why: Nothing is ambiguous to Terraform: the default applies.

choices.text: It is created in planner-dev, quietly
choices.why: Right. Which is why such a configuration names the project on every resource or uses aliases.

choices.text: Terraform guesses planner-prod from the bucket's name
choices.why: Names mean nothing to the provider.

choices.text: It is created in both projects
choices.why: One resource is one object in one project.
